risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management states agriculture 'continues to be dependent on the vagaries of temperature and rainfall' and that not only the quantity of rain but its timing is critical, with rapidly changing climatic conditions and global climate change having a drastic effect on crop performance and cropping patterns.
- Food grain production is described as heavily reliant on monsoon patterns, so irregular rainfall or extreme weather events such as droughts or floods can disrupt supply and pricing — a direct volume and margin risk for a trading and distribution business that does not control its input.
- The MD&A flags that because firms can enter and quit the industry with few limitations, the number of substitutes in the same product line at different prices poses a risk — a structural pricing-power and competitive-intensity constraint on a pure trading model.
- Explicitly listed as a threat that can adversely affect export competitiveness and import pricing.
- The Company reports that it is 'primarily engaged in Single Segment i.e. Trading and Distribution' — there is no second segment, product line or business to absorb a shock in the agri/food-grains trading cycle.
- The Board's Report states that export revenue constituted 0% of total revenue in FY 2025-26, leaving the Company entirely exposed to Indian demand, policy and monsoon conditions with no geographic diversification.
- Management states that a sustained recovery 'will depend largely on transparent, timely, and decisive policy action — elements largely outside the control of private enterprises, including those in the food grains trading sector.'
- The Board's Report confirms the Company has no holding, subsidiary or associate company and no joint venture, so there is no group balance sheet or affiliated operation to fall back on.
